This Indian politician has led the AIMIM party since 2008 and has been elected five times to the Lok Sabha from Hyderabad — who is he?
Asaduddin Owaisi (born 13 May 1969) is an Indian politician who is serving as the third and current president of the All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) since 2008.

Baudouin of Belgium (7 September 1930 - 31 July 1993) was King of the Belgians from 17 July 1951 until his death in 1993.
A Hungarian POW who embraced communism in Russia and befriended Lenin, this revolutionary returned home to govern the short-lived Hungarian Soviet Republic in 1919 — who was he?

Credited as the founder of conservatism, this Anglo-Irish writer served as a Whig member of Parliament from 1766 to 1794 and remains one of the 18th century's most influential political thinkers — name this philosopher?
Edmund Burke (12 January 1729 - 9 July 1797) was an Anglo-Irish writer, philosopher, and politician who is widely credited as the founder of the cultural and political philosophy of conservatism.
A former coca grower and union leader from an Aymara farming family, this socialist is widely regarded as Bolivia's first Indigenous president — who held the office from 2006?
Evo Morales (born 26 October 1959) is a Bolivian politician, trade union organizer, and former cocalero who served as the 65th president of Bolivia from 2006 to 2019.
Assuming the throne after Nero's suicide, this Roman emperor's brief seven-month reign made him the first of the Year of the Four Emperors. Who was he?
Galba (Latin; 24 December 3 BC - 15 January AD 69) was a Roman emperor, ruling for 7 months from 8 June AD 68 to 15 January 69.
Born in Lansing and raised in Grand Rapids, this Democratic lawyer served in both chambers of the Michigan legislature before becoming her state's 49th governor in 2019 — who is she?
Gretchen Whitmer (born August 23, 1971) is an American lawyer and politician serving as the 49th governor of Michigan since 2019.
Mother of two future English kings, this queen consort fled to her home country during the English Civil War in 1644, only to be left impoverished after her husband's execution — who is she?
Henrietta Maria of France (25 November 1609 - 10 September 1669) was Queen of England, Scotland and Ireland from her marriage to King Charles I on 13 June 1625 until his execution on 30 January 1649.

Jacob Rees-Mogg (born 24 May 1969) is a British politician, businessman and broadcaster who served as the member of Parliament (MP) for North East Somerset from 2010 to 2024.

This former assistant district attorney represented Massachusetts's 4th congressional district from 2013 to 2021 before becoming a CNN commentator and later a U.S. Special Envoy for Northern Ireland — who is he?
Joe Kennedy III (born October 4, 1980) is an American politician and former diplomat who served as the United States Special Envoy for Northern Ireland from 2022 to 2024.
The eldest son of a former prime minister, this Canadian taught secondary school in Vancouver before leading the Liberal Party and becoming his country's 23rd prime minister — who is he?
Justin Trudeau (born December 25, 1971) is a Canadian politician who served as the 23rd prime minister of Canada from 2015 to 2025.

This Romanian president previously served as mayor of Sibiu for over a decade, transforming it into one of the country's top tourist destinations and helping it become a European Capital of Culture — who is he?
Klaus Iohannis (born 13 June 1959) is a Romanian politician, physicist, and former teacher who served as the president of Romania from 2014 until his resignation in 2025.
This former co-founder of a pro wrestling empire later served as SBA administrator and then became the 13th U.S. Secretary of Education — who is she?

Linda McMahon (mk-MAN; ne Edwards; born October 4, 1948) is an American administrator, business executive and former professional wrestling executive who has served as the 13th United States secretary of education since 2025.
Before becoming Portugal's head of state in 2016, this legal scholar was already a familiar face as a TV political commentator and law professor — who is he?
Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa (born 12 December 1948) is a Portuguese politician and academic who served as the president of Portugal from 2016 to 2026.

Nicaraguan Revolution was an armed conflict that took place in the Central American nation of Nicaragua between 1961 and 1990.

Oskar Lafontaine (German; born 16 September 1943) is a German politician.
This Canadian politician has led the Conservative Party and the Official Opposition since 2022, after first being elected to Parliament in 2004. Who is he?
Pierre Poilievre (born June 3, 1979) is a Canadian politician who has served as the leader of the Conservative Party and leader of the Official Opposition since 2022.
A Russian colonel general who took over leading the Chechen Republic just after turning 30, he stepped into the role once held by his assassinated father Akhmad — who is he?

Hillsborough disaster: Fatal crowd crush during 1989 FA Cup semi-final. The Hillsborough disaster was a fatal crowd crush at a football match at Hillsborough Stadium in Sheffield, South Yorkshire, England, on 15 April 1989.

Killing of Osama bin Laden: 2011 U.S. military operation in Abbottabad, Pakistan.

What is the atomic number of Magnesium?
Magnesium is a chemical element; it has symbol Mg and atomic number 12.
In what year was Josef Mengele born?
Josef Mengele: Before the war, Mengele received doctorates in anthropology and medicine, and he began a career as a researcher.
In what year was Fructose discovered?
Fructose, or fruit sugar, is a common monosaccharide, i.e. a simple sugar.
In what year was Gallium discovered?
Gallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ga and atomic number 31.

Who is credited with discovering Scandium?
Scandium: Lars Fredrik Nilson. Scandium is a chemical element; it has symbol Sc and atomic number 21.
Despite the conspiracy buzz, this violet compound is mass-produced, sold to the public, and not a controlled substance — its hemostatic derivative is carbazochrome. What is it?
Adrenochrome is a chemical compound produced by the oxidation of adrenaline (epinephrine).
This parasitic intestinal illness, caused by Entamoeba histolytica, can produce cysts that survive for weeks in soil or nearly an hour under fingernails — what is it called?
Amoebiasis is an infection of the intestines caused by a parasitic amoeba Entamoeba histolytica.
Its Latin name means 'water-carrier,' and this zodiac constellation sits between Capricornus and Pisces, in a region of the sky nicknamed 'the Sea' for its watery neighbors — which constellation?

Aquarius (constellation) is an equatorial constellation of the zodiac, between Capricornus and Pisces. Its name is Latin for "water-carrier" or "cup-carrier", and its traditional astrological symbol is (♒︎), a representation of water.

With the symbol Ba and atomic number 56, this soft, silvery alkaline earth metal is so reactive it's never found free in nature, and takes its name from a Greek word meaning 'heavy' — name this element?
Barium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ba and atomic number 56.
Known scientifically as Simuliidae, this family of small biting insects includes more than 2,200 named species, all but a handful belonging to a single genus — what are they commonly called?
Black fly (sometimes called buffalo gnats, turkey gnats, or white socks) are flies in the family Simuliidae of the Culicomorpha infraorder.
Meaning 'thunder lizard' in Greek, this sauropod dinosaur genus was described by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1879 from a partial, skull-less skeleton found in Wyoming's Como Bluff — what dinosaur is it?

Brontosaurus (literally 'thunder lizard', from the Greek words bront, 'thunder', and saros, 'lizard') is a genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur that lived in present-day United States during the Late Jurassic period.
Its name comes from the Latin for "coal," and one of its isotopes decays with a 5,700-year half-life that lets scientists date ancient remains — which element is it?
Carbon (from Latin carbo 'coal') is a chemical element; it has symbol C and atomic number 6.

Doctors monitor blood levels every two days when giving this last-resort antibiotic, since its side effects include bone marrow suppression and, in infants, a swollen-stomach condition known as gray baby syndrome — what drug is it?
Chloramphenicol is an antibiotic useful for the treatment of a number of bacterial infections.

With just two living species — the Sunda and Philippine varieties — these Southeast Asian gliders are arboreal primatomorphs more closely related to primates than to any other animal — what is this group called?
Colugo are arboreal gliding primatomorphs that are native to Southeast Asia.

This practice and field of study focuses on techniques for secure communication in the presence of adversaries, sitting at the intersection of mathematics, computer science, and electrical engineering — what's the field called?
Cryptography is the practice and study of techniques for secure communication in the presence of adversarial behavior.
Caused by a Corynebacterium bacterium, this infection can spin a tough grey 'pseudomembrane' across the throat that slowly chokes off the airway — what is it?
Diphtheria is an infection caused by the bacterium Corynebacterium diphtheriae. The pseudomembrane can grow to cover a wide area of the throat, leading to strangulation and death.
These extinct flightless giants of Madagascar — possibly the largest birds ever, laying the biggest eggs of any amniote — vanished around 1000 AD, likely thanks to humans. What are they called?
Elephant bird are extinct flightless birds belonging to the order Aepyornithiformes that were native to the island of Madagascar.

Built by a consortium of Airbus, BAE Systems and Leonardo for four NATO nations, this twin-engine canard delta-wing fighter grew out of the 1983 Future European Fighter Aircraft programme — which jet?
Eurofighter Typhoon is a European multinational twin-engine, supersonic, canard delta wing, multirole fighter.

This genetic neurodevelopmental disorder causes a long, narrow face, large ears, and unusually flexible fingers, with males typically far more affected than females and average IQ under 55 in affected boys — what's the condition?

Fragile X syndrome (FXS) is a genetic neurodevelopmental disorder. The average IQ in males with FXS is under 55, while affected females tend to be in the borderline to normal range, typically around 70–85.

He shared a 1951 Nobel for synthesizing ten transuranium elements and developed the actinide concept that reshaped the periodic table; this American chemist later advised ten US presidents on nuclear policy — who was he?

Glenn T. Seaborg (April 19, 1912 - February 25, 1999) was an American chemist whose involvement in the synthesis, discovery and investigation of ten transuranium elements earned him a share of the 1951 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
The first Professor of the Public Understanding of Mathematics at Cambridge, she's also a BBC broadcaster who explores the math behind human relationships — who is she?
Hannah Fry (born 21 February 1984) is a British mathematician, author and broadcaster.
This common household insect, likely originating in the Middle East, mates only once in her lifetime but stores the sperm to fertilize repeated batches of about 100 eggs — what insect is it?
Housefly (Musca domestica) is a fly of the suborder Cyclorrhapha.
Patented in 1961 and approved two years later, this nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug works by blocking the enzyme cyclooxygenase to cut prostaglandin production — what drug is it?
Indometacin is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) commonly used as a prescription medication to reduce fever, pain, stiffness, and swelling from inflammation.
This British chemical engineer founded and leads a global chemicals conglomerate in 1998, and was briefly the richest person in the UK before shifting his tax residence to Monaco. Who is he?
Jim Ratcliffe (born 18 October 1952) is a British billionaire, chemical engineer, and businessman.
About the size of a domestic chicken, these flightless New Zealand natives turn out to be more closely related to Madagascar's extinct elephant birds than to the giant moa — what are they?
Kiwi (bird) are flightless birds endemic to New Zealand of the order Apterygiformes.
Found in all land animals with internal skeletons, this fibrous band connects bones to other bones and, in birds and dinosaurs, secures flight feathers in place — what is it?
Ligament is a type of fibrous connective tissue in the body that connects bones to other bones.
Found in nearly every animal cell but rare in plants, this membrane-bound organelle acts as the cell's degradation center, breaking proteins, sugars, and fats into their building blocks — what is it?
Lysosome (/lassom/) is a membrane-bound organelle that is found in all animal cells (except red blood cells), and rarely in plant cells.

Designed as both fighter and ground-attack aircraft (hence the F/A designation), this all-weather supersonic, carrier-capable twin-engined jet was derived from the YF-17 and developed for the Navy. What aircraft is this?

McDonnell Douglas F/A-18 Hornet is an all-weather supersonic, twin-engined, carrier-capable, multirole combat aircraft, designed as both a fighter and ground attack aircraft (hence the F/A designation).

Attaching to its host tree through a structure called the haustorium to steal water and nutrients, this hemiparasitic plant has one species native to the British Isles and much of Europe — what is it?
Mistletoe is the common name for obligate hemiparasitic plants in the order Santalales.
A white crystalline solid built from two fused benzene rings, this aromatic compound is the main ingredient of traditional mothballs and has an odor you can smell at just 0.08 ppm. What is it?
Naphthalene is an organic compound with the chemical formula C10H8.
Belonging to the beech family and encompassing about 500 species across the Northern Hemisphere, this hardwood tree or shrub bears a distinctive nut held in a small cup — name the tree?
Oak is a hardwood tree or shrub in the genus Quercus of the beech family.
Its name comes from the Greek for "from everywhere" because it turns up in nearly all foods — and this B vitamin lets animals build coenzyme A for energy. Which vitamin is it?
Pantothenic acid (vitamin B5) is a B vitamin and an essential nutrient.

Fill in the blank: “____ (PD) is a benign, acquired penile connective tissue disease characterized by the occurrence of fibrotic plaques within the tunica albuginea - the dense elastic covering of the corpora cavernosa.”

Peyronie's disease (PD) is a benign, acquired penile connective tissue disease characterized by the occurrence of fibrotic plaques within the tunica albuginea - the dense elastic covering of the corpora cavernosa. The plaques cause abnormal curvature, pain, penile deformities (e.g., narrowing or indentation), and usually erectile dysfunction, particularly during erection.
Carrying minor-planet number 134340, this icy Kuiper-belt world has about one-sixth the Moon's mass and got demoted when astronomers rewrote the rules — what is it?
Pluto (minor-planet number 134340) is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, a ring of bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
Belonging to the rose family, this flowering tree species gives us most plums, including the greengage and damson varieties — which species is it?
Prunus domestica is a species of flowering plant in the family Rosaceae.
With roughly 12,000 living species split across four classic orders — including the single-species tuatara branch — what ectothermic class is this?
Reptile are tetrapod vertebrate animals with an ectothermic metabolism and amniotic development.

Known from complete specimens found in Bolivia, this extinct armored jawless fish from the Ordovician period resembled a slender tadpole with eyes set like car headlamps on its oversized head — what is it?
Sacabambaspis is an extinct genus of armored jawless fish which lived in the Ordovician period.

Essentially plasma with the clotting factors and cells removed, this pale yellow fluid still carries antibodies, hormones, and electrolytes and is central to typing tests done before a transfusion — what is it?
Serum (blood) is the fluid and solvent component of blood which does not play a role in clotting.
This use of the human voice for language ranges from informing and persuading to simply asking or declaring, combining vowels and consonants into meaningful words — what is it called?
Speech is the use of the human voice as a medium for language.
Among the most experienced spacewalkers in history, this NASA astronaut logged over 62 hours across nine spacewalks — the most of any woman — who is she?
Sunita Williams (ne Pandya; born September 19, 1965) is a retired United States Navy captain and former NASA astronaut.
Raised in Michigan with little schooling, he sold his first inventions by age 22 and moved to New York to chase engineering — going on to become one of America's most famous inventors. Who?
Thomas Edison (February 11, 1847 - October 18, 1931) was an American inventor and businessman.
First isolated as a metal in 1783, this element is drawn from ores like scheelite and wolframite — the latter lending it an alternative name. Which metal is it?
Tungsten (also called wolfram) is a chemical element; it has symbol W (from) and atomic number 74.
Named from a French verb meaning 'to see,' this term describes the practice of secretly watching others in intimate moments, often labeled 'Peeping Tom' behavior — what is it?
Voyeurism is the habit of clandestine watching other people engaged in intimate behaviors, such as undressing, sexual activity, or other actions of a private nature, commonly for sexual stimulation.

Nicknamed the 'Sleeping Dragon' during his years in seclusion, this Chinese strategist was sought out three times by a warlord before becoming chancellor of the Shu Han state and, later, regent to its young second emperor — who is he?

Zhuge Liang (181 AD - September or October 234 AD), courtesy name Kongming, was a Chinese statesman and strategist who lived through the collapse of the Eastern Han dynasty and became the principal architect of the Shu Han state.
This nucleoside, a building block of RNA, gives rise to the energy carriers ATP and ADP and is used as an intravenous drug for certain irregular heartbeats — what is it?
Working at a Soviet computing centre in 1985, this engineer designed one of history's most famous puzzle games — yet saw no royalties from it until founding a company around it in 1996. Who is he?
Domesticated in Southwest China roughly 2,000 years ago, this corm-producing plant is nicknamed 'devil's tongue' and gets boiled down into a jelly-like noodle called shirataki — what is it?
Amorphophallus konjac: Edible plant from Yunnan, China.
NATO code-named 'Condor,' this Soviet-designed four-engine giant is the largest military transport aircraft still flying today — which aircraft?

Antonov An-124 Ruslan: Soviet military transport aircraft. Assembly of the first aircraft begun in 1979; the An-124 (which was sometimes referred to as the An-40 in the West) performed its maiden flight on 24 December 1982.
Most commonly caused by liver cirrhosis and its resulting high blood pressure in the portal system, this condition is the abnormal buildup of fluid in the abdominal cavity — which one?
Ascites: Abnormal build-up of fluid in the abdomen.
Instead of teeth, these marine mammals sieve plankton through whalebone plates in their mouths — a group of 16 species that includes the rorquals and the bowhead. What do we call them?
Both heads of this upper-arm muscle originate on the scapula and let you flex your elbow while turning your palm upward — what muscle is it?

Biceps: Muscle on the front of the upper arm. While the long head of the biceps crosses both the shoulder and elbow joints, its main function is at the elbow where it flexes and supinates the forearm.

Developed in the 1980s-90s to replace an aging Cold War transport aircraft, this large military cargo plane carries forward the name of two earlier piston-engined predecessors, the C-74 and C-124. What is this modern behemoth called?
Boeing C-17 Globemaster III: American four engine military transport aircraft.

Affecting roughly 22% of people worldwide, this oral parafunctional habit — often during sleep and without the person's awareness — can leave you with aching jaw muscles, headaches, and worn-down teeth. What is it?
Bruxism: Grinding or clenching of the teeth.
Once used in Italy for hunting large game and herding cattle, this mastiff breed today mostly serves as a guard dog or companion — which breed?
Cane Corso: Italian breed of mastiff. It is usually kept as a companion dog or guard dog; it may also be used to protect livestock.
Marked by patients who may lie motionless for days or repeat purposeless movements, this neuropsychiatric syndrome often responds to benzodiazepines or electroconvulsive therapy — which condition?
Domesticated from the red junglefowl roughly 8,000 years ago, this bird now numbers over 26 billion worldwide, more than any other domesticated species — what is it?
Chicken: Domesticated subspecies of red junglefowl. The chicken (Gallus gallus domesticus) is the domesticated form of the red junglefowl (Gallus gallus), originally native to Southeast Asia.
Sold under the brand name Anafranil, this tricyclic antidepressant treats obsessive-compulsive disorder but also premature ejaculation and the cataplexy that comes with narcolepsy — which drug?
Clomipramine: Antidepressant. It has also been notably used to treat premature ejaculation and the cataplexy associated with narcolepsy.
Once classified among the thrushes, this small Old World flycatcher was later reassigned to the family Muscicapidae — which bird?
Common redstart: Species of bird. The common redstart (Phoenicurus phoenicurus), or often simply redstart, is a small passerine bird in the genus Phoenicurus.
First identified in Europe and interbreeding with Neanderthals as early as roughly 45,000 years ago, this term describes the earliest known modern humans on the continent — what are they called?
Cro-Magnon: Earliest anatomically modern humans in Europe and West Asia.
In 1900, this mathematician presented a list of unsolved problems that shaped 20th-century mathematical research — who is he?
This linguistic term describes a combination of two vowel sounds gliding together within a single syllable, as heard five times in the phrase 'no highway cowboys' — what is it called?

Diphthong: Combination of two adjacent vowel sounds. A diphthong ( DIF-thong, DIP-), also known as a gliding vowel or a vowel glide, is a combination of two adjacent vowel sounds within the same syllable.
Starting life bilaterally symmetrical as larvae but growing into five-pointed radial adults, this animal phylum includes starfish, sea urchins, and sea cucumbers — what is it called?
Echinoderm: Marine phylum of animals often with radial symmetries.
This branch of zoology, whose name derives from Greek words for 'insect' and 'study,' covers a field that has described over 1.3 million species — which discipline?
The only Old World member of its family to breed in the Northern Hemisphere's temperate zones, this migratory songbird winters in central and southern Africa — what is it?
Eurasian golden oriole: Species of bird.
This Swiss thinker, alongside Charles Sanders Peirce, is considered one of the two founders of semiotics — the field he himself called 'semiology' — who is he?
Ferdinand de Saussure: Swiss linguist and philosopher (1857–1913)
Marked by physical traits such as a long face, large ears, and unusually flexible fingers, this inherited neurodevelopmental disorder stems from a repeat expansion in the FMR1 gene — which condition?
Fragile X syndrome: X-linked dominant genetic disorder.
This is the largest lizard family, boasting over 950 species that cling to surfaces via Van der Waals forces in their toe hairs — including house, tokay, and day varieties — which family?
Gekkonidae: Family of lizards. Gekkonidae (the common geckos) is the largest family of geckos, containing over 950 described species in 62 genera.
With the symbol Au and atomic number 79, this soft, dense element is so unreactive that only platinum sits below it — and it often turns up as native nuggets in riverbeds. What is it?
Gold: Chemical element with atomic number 79 (Au). Chemically, gold is a transition metal, a group 11 element, and one of the noble metals.
Caused by a hormone imbalance between estrogens and androgens, which benign condition results in enlarged breast tissue in men?
Gynecomastia: Enlargement of the human male breast.
Dubbed 'the Gauss of modern mathematics,' this French polymath's work on the three-body problem uncovered the first chaotic deterministic system, laying the groundwork for chaos theory — who is he?
Henri Poincaré: French mathematician, physicist and engineer (1854–1912)
With red compound eyes set wider apart in females, this insect lays batches of about 100 eggs on decaying matter that hatch into maggots — which species?
Housefly: Species of insect. The housefly (Musca domestica) is a fly of the suborder Cyclorrhapha.
This family of long-legged wading birds that live in wetlands and forests lent its name — mistakenly — to the scientific name of the western cattle egret in 1757 — what's the bird group called?
Ibis: Long-legged wading birds with down-curved beaks.
This Russian physiologist won the 1904 Nobel Prize for his work on digestion, but is far better remembered for training dogs to salivate at a signal — who was he?
Building his first firearm at age 13 in his father's gun shop, this American designer earned 128 patents and pioneered the autoloading pistol — who is he?
Marketed as Nizoral, this antifungal medication also treats Cushing's syndrome and excess hair growth in women, though oral use risks liver damage — which drug?
This probability principle explains why a casino might lose money on a single spin of roulette but reliably earns a predictable percentage over many thousands of spins. What is it called?
Law of large numbers: Averages of repeated trials converge to the expected value.
Patented in 1978 and approved for use in the US in 1987, this ACE inhibitor is a common first-line treatment for high blood pressure — what drug is it?
Lisinopril: Medication used to treat hypertension and heart failure.
Named from a Greek root meaning 'light' or 'brightness' in reference to its luminous, reflective eyes, this genus includes the bobcat among its four wild cat species — which genus?
Lynx: Genus of medium-sized wild cats.
A Russian pediatric endocrinologist also known by the surname Faassen, this woman is the elder child of Russia's president. Who is she?
Maria Vorontsova: Daughter of Vladimir Putin (born 1985)
This mammal family — skunks and stink badgers — was reclassified out of the weasel family in the 1990s after genetic evidence, and turns out to be closest kin to red pandas and raccoons. What is it?
Mephitidae: Family of mammals. In taxonomic order, the living species of Mephitidae are:.

The only woman among Einstein's classmates at Zurich Polytechnic, this Serbian mathematician was his first wife and is still debated as a possible collaborator on his 1905 miracle-year papers. Who was she?
Mileva Marić: Wife of Albert Einstein (1875–1948)
Grown above the upper lip and below the nose, this facial hair style has taken many forms across history — what is it called?
Moustache: Strip of facial hair across the upper lip. A moustache (UK:) or mustache (US:) is a growth of facial hair grown above the upper lip and under the nose of men.

Attributed to 19th-century pathologist Rudolf Virchow, this term for the premature death of cells caused by trauma or infection contrasts with the body's own programmed cell death — what's the condition called?
Necrosis: Unprogrammed cell death caused by external cell injury.
A subsonic flying wing with a crew of two to three, this nuclear-capable stealth aircraft was built to slip past sophisticated air defenses for the US Air Force — what is it?
Northrop B-2 Spirit: American heavy strategic bomber.
Named by analogy to how organs serve the body, what term describes a specialized, function-specific subunit within a biological cell?

Organelle: Specialized subunit within a cell. The name organelle comes from the idea that these structures are parts of cells, as organs are to the body, hence organelle, the suffix -elle being a diminutive.
Sold under the brand name Paxil, this SSRI antidepressant treats conditions from panic disorder to PTSD, and is also prescribed for premature ejaculation and menopausal hot flashes — what is it?
Paroxetine: SSRI antidepressant. It has also been used in the treatment of premature ejaculation, and hot flashes due to menopause.
Secreted by eccrine and apocrine glands, this bodily fluid can flow at up to 4 litres per hour in adults and cools the body via evaporation — what is it?
Perspiration: Fluid secreted from sudoriferous glands.

Cultivated for its edible nuts since prehistoric times and native to the Mediterranean and the Levant, this pine species has earned the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit — which species?
Pinus pinea: Species of pine tree. Pinus pinea, the Italian stone pine or Mediterranean stone pine, is a tree from the pine family, Pinaceae.
Stockpiled for radiation emergencies, this oral compound floods and shields the thyroid gland — and also treats hyperthyroidism and the skin infection sporotrichosis. Which compound is it?
Fossils of this genus, found in Germany's Solnhofen limestone, mark the first pterosaur ever identified as a flying reptile — which genus?
Pterodactylus: Genus of pterodactyloid pterosaur from the Late Jurassic.
Belonging to the genus Corvus and distinguished from its close relatives mainly by size, the largest species in this bird category are also the largest of all perching birds — which bird?
Raven: Index of animals with the same common name.
This Israeli-American mathematician shared the 2005 Nobel in Economics with Thomas Schelling for illuminating conflict and cooperation through game theory — who is he?
Named for the genus of the Atlantic salmon, this family of cold-water fish also includes trout, char, and grayling — what family is it?
As chief technology officer of a Turkish defense company, this pilot-engineer designed Turkey's first indigenous unmanned combat aerial vehicle and its first unmanned fighter jet. Who is he?
Selçuk Bayraktar: Turkish engineer and businessman. Selçuk Bayraktar (born 7 October 1979) is a Turkish pilot, engineer and businessman.
Related to polecats but more closely kin to the Old World stink badgers, these black-and-white mammals defend themselves by spraying a foul-smelling liquid from their anal glands — which animal?
Skunk: Common name of mammals in the family Mephitidae.
Lacking any nervous, digestive, or circulatory system, these ancient sea-bound filter feeders pump water through pore-riddled bodies using flagella to survive — what are they?
Sponge: Animals of the phylum Porifera.
Nicknamed the "Super Flanker" and derived from the Su-27, this twin-engine, supermaneuverable Russian air superiority fighter first flew as a prototype in 1988 — what is it?
Sukhoi Su-35: Upgraded series of the Su-27 fighter aircraft.
Nicknamed the brown raptor, this nocturnal bird of prey nests in tree hollows across Europe and is so territorial that evicted youngsters may starve — what is it?
Tawny owl: Stocky medium-sized owl species.

When a piece of one of these blood-vessel clots breaks free to travel the body it's called an embolus — and the original blockage can trigger a stroke or heart attack. What is this clot formation called?
Thrombosis: Formation of blood clots inside the blood vessels.
Also known as all-trans retinoic acid, this medication treats acne as a topical cream but must be taken orally for leukemia patients with a specific gene fusion — what is it?
Tretinoin: Medication. Tretinoin, also known as all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA), is a medication used for the treatment of acne and acute promyelocytic leukemia.
Home to Polaris, the North Star, this far-northern constellation is also nicknamed the Little Dipper — which one?
Ursa Minor: Constellation in the northern celestial hemisphere.
Born in Omaha to a U.S. congressman, this investor chairs Berkshire Hathaway and ranked as the world's ninth-richest person in early 2026 — who is he?
Warren Buffett: American investor and philanthropist (born 1930)
One of Europe's largest bee species, this dark, iridescent carpenter bee nests in dead wood and is generally not aggressive unless provoked — which insect?
Xylocopa violacea: Species of bee. Xylocopa violacea, the violet carpenter bee, is the common European species of carpenter bee, and one of the largest bees in Europe.
